chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Do not look in the mirror while you are in the state of Ihram, for it is from adornment."

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram, a sacred state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on looking in a mirror while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the prohibition of mirror-gazing to the concept of *zinah* (adornment), extending the general Ihram restrictions on wearing sewn garments and using perfume to include visual self-adornment. This ruling highlights the spiritual objective of Ihram: to strip away worldly vanity and maintain a state of humble devotion, ensuring that the pilgrim’s focus remains on God rather than personal appearance. The hadith reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the spirit of Ihram encompasses both physical and aesthetic simplicity.
